# HTTP contracts, validation and MVC state

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `aspnet-http-contracts` · **ASP.NET Core & API Engineering** · Catalog level: foundation

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S02-Q013](#S02-Q013)

<p>Which HTTP method would you choose for a file-upload operation, and which operation semantics justify it?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Define an HTTP interaction contract whose method, response and state choices match one caller workflow.</p>

<ul>
<li>Separate API and page-rendering responsibilities for a client.</li>
<li>Choose an HTTP method and redirect contract from intended operation semantics.</li>
<li>Place validation and define actionable invalid-input responses.</li>
<li>Choose state lifetime and ownership, accounting for concurrent calls and replicas.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>First separate API and page-delivery responsibilities. Redirect and MVC state questions then expose how a client continues an interaction; upload and validation questions apply those contracts to input. REST and session trade-offs ask whether the contract remains suitable as caller and deployment constraints change. These questions share one decision: what a caller can rely on across requests, rather than which framework feature is fashionable.</p>

<a id="S02-Q011"></a>

### S02-Q011 · Foundation

<p>How do a RESTful API and a server-rendered MVC application differ in responsibilities and client interaction?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q011](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q011)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q011](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q011)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What is the difference between RESTful APIs and server-rendered MVC?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare two delivery styles for the same user action. REST is an architectural style, so explain the intended contract rather than reducing the distinction to a response format.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Separate API and page-rendering responsibilities without confusing architectural levels.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume HTTP and one business capability; an MVC application may also expose APIs. No specific framework default is implied.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace where presentation and application responsibilities sit in each design.</li>
<li>Explain one client or deployment constraint that changes the choice.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating REST with any JSON endpoint or claiming MVC and REST cannot coexist.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would supporting a mobile client affect your design?</li>
<li>What changes if the same application serves pages and APIs?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q015"></a>

### S02-Q015 · Mechanism

<p>Which HTTP status codes express redirection, and how do temporary and permanent redirects differ for clients?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q015](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q015)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q015](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q015)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Which HTTP status codes represent redirects and how do temporary and permanent redirects differ?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare the semantics relevant to a browser or API client, including method handling and future use of the target URL. Distinguish intended protocol semantics from client observations.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Select a redirect contract and identify client behavior to verify.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the original method, client and caching context; consult official HTTP specifications and the actual framework documentation before asserting behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Compare relevant redirect codes rather than only their numeric labels.</li>
<li>Propose a client test for method/body handling and cached redirects.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating all 3xx responses as interchangeable or ignoring request-method behavior.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you test when redirecting a request with a body?</li>
<li>How would you change a redirect that a client may have cached?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q016 · Mechanism

<p>How do ViewData, ViewBag and TempData differ in an MVC application, and which would you use for a stated message or view value?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q016](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q016)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q016](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q016)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain `ViewData`, `ViewBag`, and `TempData` in MVC-style applications.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the data handoff and intended lifetime in a concrete render or redirect flow. Avoid treating these conveniences as interchangeable business-data stores.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a view-state mechanism from access and lifetime requirements.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify ASP.NET Core MVC or older MVC, version and TempData provider; verify official lifetime and consumption rules.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace where the value is written and read in the chosen flow.</li>
<li>Explain a missing-value case and why longer-lived data belongs elsewhere.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Reciting names without showing lifetime or assuming all providers behave identically.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would a redirect change the lifetime requirement?</li>
<li>How would you test a value read more than once?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S02-Q010 · Application

<p>How would you validate an incoming API model before allowing its business operation to proceed?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q010](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q010)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q010](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q010)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should validation be implemented for incoming models?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Distinguish input shape and field rules from business rules that depend on current system state. Explain the invalid-input response the caller can act on.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Place validation responsibilities and define an observable failure contract.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name ASP.NET Core version, endpoint model and validation configuration; verify automatic behavior in official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace malformed, structurally valid and business-invalid input separately.</li>
<li>Explain where state-dependent rules run and test error consistency.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming field annotations alone cover database races and every business invariant.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What if input passes validation but relevant data changes before persistence?</li>
<li>How would you keep errors consistent across several endpoints?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q013"></a>

### S02-Q013 · Application

<p>Which HTTP method would you choose for a file-upload operation, and which operation semantics justify it?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q013](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q013)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q013](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q013)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Which HTTP method should be used for file upload and why?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Clarify whether the caller creates an upload resource or replaces a known resource. The question concerns the operation contract, not only transferring file bytes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an HTTP method from resource identity and retry semantics.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State resource ownership, overwrite behavior and retry expectations; consult official HTTP and framework documentation for the selected method and upload API.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explain the resource affected and the intended effect of repetition.</li>
<li>Define response semantics and test an interrupted or repeated upload.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Choosing a method only because it supports a request body.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How does an existing caller-chosen resource ID affect the decision?</li>
<li>What should a client do after losing the upload response?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q012"></a>

### S02-Q012 · Trade-offs

<p>What advantages and trade-offs would a REST API introduce for a concrete product capability?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q012](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q012)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q012](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q012)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What are the advantages and trade-offs of REST APIs?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Choose a caller and interaction pattern, then judge the style against their requirements. Discuss costs and limits alongside benefits instead of giving a universal recommendation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Evaluate an API style against a stated workload and operational constraints.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use HTTP, a specified client and a concrete read/write workflow; distinguish architectural properties from implementation promises.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Tie benefits and costs to the chosen interaction pattern.</li>
<li>Name an alternative and the evidence or requirement that would favor it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming REST is always faster or scalable merely because responses are JSON.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Would frequent server-pushed updates change your choice?</li>
<li>How would you validate the number and cost of client round trips?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S02-Q014"></a>

### S02-Q014 · Trade-offs

<p>When is session state appropriate for an HTTP application, and what constraints make it a poor fit?</p>

**Source:** [S02-Q014](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q014)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S02-Q014](../../sources/02-aspnet-api-ef.md#q014)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When is session state appropriate?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Session state associates data with interactions from a caller across requests. Clarify which data needs that lifetime and what happens if it is lost or unavailable.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose state ownership from consistency, lifetime and deployment needs.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the framework version, session provider and replica topology; verify provider persistence and concurrency behavior in official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Classify the proposed data by lifetime and business criticality.</li>
<li>Explain an outage or replica-switch scenario and compare an alternative store.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating session as a durable system of record without examining its guarantees.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would two concurrent requests affect the chosen session data?</li>
<li>What happens if the next request reaches another replica?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Agent-added production exercise: a web workflow uploads a document, shows validation errors or a success message, and can continue on another application replica. Define the upload method, invalid-input response and any redirect; identify each value that must survive another request and who owns it. Compare browser and API-client behavior, then propose tests for a repeated upload, concurrent requests and a replica switch. Check official HTTP/framework/provider semantics before claiming them.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Names plausible methods and status codes, distinguishes pages from APIs, and explains basic validation and transient state.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Connects every choice to resource identity and caller behavior; accounts for redirects, repeat calls, invalid input and state loss; defends an alternative under changed requirements.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A list of status codes or state APIs is insufficient. Need a coherent request/response trace, client tests or a documented validation plan for the chosen provider.</p>
